sampling: Split the body into 316 blank-line paragraphs (fenced blocks whole, Sources included); offset 0, stride 3; 15 claims, 9 numbers; each checked against the live docs page, SDK 2.60 source/CLI help, the cited blog, or by running the guide's code.

score_evidence.A: Real tables, fenced code, absolute images with Korean alt (L605), no math so no use_math. Deductions: no TL;DR (L10 opens '소개와 설치'); topic-name headings (L205, L599, L664, L683, L854, L1414); architecture at L599 after the whole tutorial; the post ends with a further-reading list (L1545) rather than a closing section.
score_evidence.B: Natural, readable Korean with varied sentence shapes and few calques. Deductions: '배포' covers both deployment and deploy, e.g. L1052 '애플리케이션은 배포가 목표 레플리카 수에 도달하지 못한 동안' (rewrite: '디플로이먼트가 목표 레플리카 수에 이르기 전까지 애플리케이션은 DEPLOYING 상태입니다'); some '할 수 있습니다' where things simply happen (L445, L1289).
score_evidence.C: Follows a clean learning order (plain class -> deployment -> run -> compose -> architecture -> config -> scaling -> production -> multi-app -> routing -> monitoring) with explicit back-references that resolve. Deductions: file-name drift (L984 config.yaml vs L1048 serve_config.yaml), text_ml.py assumed at L1016 but never written; L178 overwrites the model.py from L61.
score_evidence.D: Help lands where it is hard: the max_ongoing_requests experiment with three predicted timings (L635-662), the 20-user autoscaling calculation (L942), the 30 s/600 s asymmetry rationale (L957), the response-object table (L593). Deductions: basics get padding (pre-Serve Translator L53-101, the status walkthrough L288-292), and the L660 sync-handler prediction misleads.
score_evidence.E: Tables are well chosen (decorator args L152, config defaults L693, autoscaling knobs L946, REST endpoints L1060, response objects L593, symptom->view L1463); architecture and autoscaling diagrams placed where discussed (L605, L936); FastAPI and get_app_handle shown as diffs (L178, L1268) instead of full repeats. Minor: the composed Translator body is printed again at L314.
score_evidence.F: APIs, flags and defaults match docs, SDK 2.60 and CLI help (see claims). Deductions: L660 '약 6초' prediction for sync handlers is contradicted by running the guide's own script (3.6 s / 1.0 s) (-2); L752 import path copied from a docs mismatch so the YAML cannot load.
score_evidence.T1: Almost every no-GPU block ran: hello, model.py, quickstart, FastAPI, composition, parallel calls, chain, stream, ObjectRef, the timing script, reconfigure, autoscale, serve build, multi-app with get_app_handle, the custom router app. Deductions: L749-764 YAML import path fails; text_ml.py and serve_config.yaml are referenced but never created; the REST example's external zip breaks on transformers 5.
score_evidence.T2: Grounded in the sources and ordered for learning; covers getting started, composition, architecture, configuration, autoscaling (incl. advanced knobs), production config, REST API, KubeRay, multi-app, custom routing, dashboard and registries without padding.
score_evidence.T3: Internals are present and often explained with reasons (why controller is off the data path L613/L681, two queues and backpressure L623, autoscaler metric window and delays L938-961, Serve vs Ray autoscaler L965-973, router placement and consistency L1385/L1397). Deductions: they arrive late (L599) after a long tutorial; few non-official design sources (15%); no closing on when to choose Serve, alternatives, or a failure-mode summary.

examples.claim: Unlike framework-specific tools such as TorchServe, Serve does no model-specific optimisation
examples.source: serve/index.html FAQ 'TFServing, TorchServe, ONNXRuntime': Serve 'doesn't perform any model-specific optimizations'

examples.claim: max_ongoing_requests defaults to 5; it changed from 100 to 5 in Ray 2.32.0
examples.source: configure-serve-deployment.html: 'Defaults to 5 (note the default changed from 100 to 5 in Ray 2.32.0)'

examples.claim: With def and time.sleep(1) the replica stalls per request, so six requests take about 6 s regardless of the limit
examples.source: Ran the guide's L637 script on ray 2.60 with def/time.sleep(1): 3.6 s at max_ongoing_requests=2 and 1.0 s at 6. architecture.html does say 'Otherwise, the replica blocks until the handler returns', but the 6 s figure is the writer's own and is contradicted by running the guide's own code.

examples.source: architecture.html FAQ: 'Larger request objects (100KiB+) ... zero-copy read'
